# Implementation Procedure: tests/mcp_servers/test_mcp_dispatch.py

<!-- Generated by plan-to-implementation-procedure from plans/20261007-163229_plan.md -->
<!-- Source plan timestamp marker: 20261007-180245 -->

## Goal

Add unit tests covering the rewritten `dispatch_tool()` cache behavior so every
Acceptance criterion for the cache is exercised (REQ-001..REQ-004).

## Scope

- Modify `tests/mcp_servers/test_mcp_dispatch.py` only.
- Covers REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004 (test coverage only).
- Add a new test class (or methods) alongside the existing `TestDispatchTool`.

## Assumptions

- Caching only applies to side-effecting tools, so tests must dispatch a
  side-effecting tool name (verified via `_is_side_effecting`) with an
  `idempotency_key`.
- `_duplicate_cache` is a module-level dict that tests can clear between cases to
  isolate each scenario.
- Cache TTL / max-entry constants are implementation-defined (UNK-02); tests should
  reference the real constants or make them patchable rather than hardcoding
  durations.

## Design decisions

- Clear `_duplicate_cache` in a fixture / at the start of each cache test to avoid
  cross-test contamination.
- Drive the cache path by passing a side-effecting tool name and an explicit
  `idempotency_key` to `dispatch_tool`.
- For TTL/eviction, reference the implementation's own constants (or monkeypatch
  them) so tests do not depend on wall-clock waits or fragile magic numbers.

## Alternatives considered

- **Hardcode a fake side-effecting name:** rejected — the cache gate depends on
  `_is_side_effecting(name)` (line 63/99), so the name must be a genuine member of
  the write/dangerous/exec set. Import `_is_side_effecting` (or the underlying
  tool set) and select a real member.
- **Test via a public wrapper:** rejected — the cache is internal to
  `dispatch_tool`; test it directly through `dispatch_tool` with a key.

## Implementation

### Target file

`tests/mcp_servers/test_mcp_dispatch.py`

### Procedure

1. Import `_duplicate_cache` and `_is_side_effecting` from
   `mcp_servers.dispatch` (extend the existing import at lines 5-8).
2. Add a cache-behavior test class with a setup step that clears
   `_duplicate_cache` before each case.
3. Add these cases (each dispatches a side-effecting tool with an
   `idempotency_key`, except the None/empty-key case):
   - Empty string and `None` key: handler runs every time; `_duplicate_cache`
     stays empty (REQ-001).
   - Same key + same tool + same args dispatched twice: handler runs once; second
     call returns the cached result (REQ-002 / Acceptance line 87).
   - Same key, different tool name: second call is rejected as an error result
     (REQ-002 / Acceptance line 87).
   - Same key, different args: second call is rejected as an error result
     (REQ-002).
   - TTL expiry: after the TTL elapses, a repeat call re-executes (REQ-003).
   - Eviction: exceeding the max entry count evicts the oldest entry; an evicted
     key re-executes on next call (REQ-003).
   - Error result not cached: a handler raising `ValueError` does not populate the
     cache; a subsequent identical call re-executes (REQ-004).
   - `dry_run` result not cached: a `dry_run` result does not populate the cache
     (REQ-004 / UNK-01 resolution).
4. Keep the new async test style consistent with the existing
   `@pytest.mark.asyncio` methods (lines 12-84).

### Method

- Use plain in-line async handlers that record call counts (e.g. a mutable list
  or counter) to assert how many times the handler actually executed.
- Assert both the returned `DispatchResult` (served vs. rejected) and the handler
  execution count.

### Details

- Existing `TestDispatchTool` never passes an `idempotency_key` and never uses a
  side-effecting tool name (plan line 59), so the cache branch is currently
  untested — these new cases are the first coverage of that path.
- For the rejection case, assert `result.is_error is True` and that the handler
  did NOT run a second time.

## Compatibility considerations

- New tests are additive; existing `TestDispatchTool` methods are untouched.
- Clearing `_duplicate_cache` is scoped to the new test class only.

## Security considerations

- N/A: test-only change; no secrets or I/O introduced.
